The differential equation that generates the slope field shown above is given by ${y}^{′}=-(x-a)(x-b).$ Find the value of $a+b.$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14044310/assets/1da6182ac4999453b1c7e5f4c7db4d0a7e42f285463e8fe35aac5b8df46eb400.png)

 

Notice that the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=-2$ and $x=4,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines.

So, our differential equation must be

$$
{y}^{′}=-(x+2)(x-4).
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $a=-2,b=4$ and $a+b=2.$
